core_principles.text: The movement should start with the elbow joint in full extension, flexing the forearm until the dumbbells reach the top of the shoulders, and then returning to the starting position.
The elbows must be kept close to the body during the movement.

specific_findings.text: In a simulation comparing dumbbell curls with 6 kg and 10.7 kg, the rate of increase of elbow peak moment was 57.7% and the rate of increase of peak muscle force was 38.3%.
Increasing the dumbbell load from 6 kg to 10.7 kg resulted in a 44.4% increase in maximum strain and a 37.3% increase in maximum stress in the biceps brachii finite element model.
Biomechanical analysis indicates that increasing the dumbbell load does not increase the muscle force of the biceps brachii at the same rate.

core_principles.text: The muscle moment arm distance changes during the dumbbell curl exercise, which means that increasing the exercise load does not scale muscle contraction or mechanical response at a linear rate.

specific_findings.text: The peak joint moment was calculated to be 18.88 Nm with a 6 kg dumbbell and 29.78 Nm with a 10.7 kg dumbbell.
The peak muscle force of the biceps brachii was calculated to be 645.66 N with a 6 kg dumbbell and 893.04 N with a 10.7 kg dumbbell.
Comparing 6 kg and 10.7 kg dumbbells, the rate of increase of load was 78.3%, the rate of increase of peak joint moment was 57.7%, and the rate of increase of peak muscle force was 38.3%.
Maximum strain on the tendon was calculated as 4.44 mm/mm with a 6 kg dumbbell and 6.42 mm/mm with a 10.7 kg dumbbell.
The mean maximum stress (σmax) was 4.85 MPa with a 6 kg dumbbell and 7.46 MPa with a 10.7 kg dumbbell, while the peak value of σmax was 7.76 MPa and 10.66 MPa, respectively.
Comparing the two loads, the rate of increase of maximum stress was 44.4% and the rate of increase of maximum strain was 37.3%.
